subtitle: Lesson 13 · Technical Leadership & Influence

code:
You can see the likely cause almost
immediately -- a race condition between
retrieval and prompt-assembly.

Fast move: just say so.

Cost: the bug gets fixed. The skill of
finding the next one never gets practiced.
caption: You practiced the debugging for them, not with them.

eyebrow: A structure that actually builds capability

steps.label: Ask what they've tried
steps.sub: Avoids repeating a ruled-out idea; tells you their real approach

steps.label: Ask a narrowing question
steps.sub: Points toward the cause without naming it -- models the transferable skill

steps.label: Let a wrong hypothesis sit
steps.sub: Ruling it out themselves teaches more, if the cost is genuinely low

steps.label: Give the answer if truly stuck
steps.sub: Explain the reasoning that gets there, not just the conclusion

code:
Stuck 20 minutes, hasn't considered
an obvious angle
   -> usually benefits from a nudge.

Stuck 2 days, behind on a deadline
that affects other people, already
tried everything
   -> withholding the answer now is
      a cost, not mentorship.
caption: Reading which situation you're in is itself part of the skill.

eyebrow: Letting a bounded wrong turn happen
code:
They're convinced their fix belongs
in one spot; you can see a cleaner
spot three calls away.

Implementing it, hitting the
awkwardness, and figuring out why --
often teaches more than redirecting
them first.
caption: Only works when the detour costs a few hours, not a shipped production bug.
